title: All-section and transport comparisons over an inner-horn completion
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor categories and coherent natural equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the smallness convention of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and cocartesian fibrations over arbitrary simplicial bases and marked inverse equivalences as in [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. Fix an uncountable regular cardinal $\kappa$. Let $i:X\hookrightarrow X'$ be a monomorphism of $\kappa$-small simplicial sets, with $X'$ a quasicategory, obtained as a countable composite of pushouts of coproducts of inner horn inclusions $\Lambda_j^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<j<n$. Let $q:Y\to X$ and $q':Y'\to X'$ be cocartesian fibrations, and suppose $u:Y\to i^*Y'$ over $X$ preserves cocartesian edges and has an inverse up to coherent natural equivalences over $X$, also preserving cocartesian edges. The total spaces may be arbitrarily large in a fixed containing universe. Write $\Gamma(q)_n=\{s:X\times\Delta^n\to Y\mid qs=\operatorname{pr}_X\}$, and similarly for the other fibrations.The simplicial sets $\Gamma(q)$, $\Gamma(i^*q')$ and $\Gamma(q')$ are quasicategories. Postcomposition $u_*:\Gamma(q)\to\Gamma(i^*q')$ and restriction $i^*:\Gamma(q')\to\Gamma(i^*q')$ are functor equivalences; restriction has the right lifting property against every simplicial monomorphism in the containing universe. For every vertex $x\in X$, $u$ gives a fiber equivalence $u_x:Y_x\to Y'_{i(x)}$, and the identities $\operatorname{ev}_x u_*=u_x\operatorname{ev}_x$ and $\operatorname{ev}_x i^*=\operatorname{ev}_{i(x)}$ hold. Thus quasi-inverses give evaluation squares commuting up to coherent natural equivalence.For every old edge $e:x\to z$, the fiber equivalences intertwine its transport functors up to coherent natural equivalence. Here transport along an edge means a functor on the initial fiber with a cylinder into the total space over that edge, restricting to the initial inclusion and the final fiber inclusion composed with the functor, whose vertex edges are cocartesian. Let $\mathcal J$ be any collection of quasicategorical indexing shapes in the containing universe. If every fiber of $q$ admits all $J$-indexed colimits for $J\in\mathcal J$ and every edge transport of $q$ preserves them, then every fiber of $q'$ admits these colimits and every edge transport of $q'$ preserves them. No filteredness of fibers or section categories is assumed or asserted.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.4.2, opening base-replacement argument; Corollary 3.3.1.2, Proposition 3.3.1.5, Proposition 2.3.2.4 and cocartesian composition in Proposition 2.4.1.7; all-section and new-edge preservation comparisons expanded from the returned Step 2. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial or quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: The given inclusion is a countable composite of pushouts of coproducts of inner horn inclusions, hence it has the left lifting property against every inner fibration by the inner-horn cell-generation theorem; every inner horn inclusion is itself in this class. Since $X'$ is a quasicategory and $q'$ is an inner fibration, $Y'$ is a quasicategory: an inner horn in $Y'$ is filled first in $X'$ and then lifted along $q'$. No such claim is made for $Y$: $X$ need not be a quasicategory, and then neither need $Y$ be (for $X=Y=\Lambda^2_1\subset X'=Y'=\Delta^2$ with identity maps all hypotheses hold and $Y$ is not a quasicategory). For every vertex $x$ of $X$, however, the fiber $Y_x=Y\times_X\{x\}$ is a quasicategory, since every inner horn in it lies over a degenerate simplex of $X$ and is filled over that simplex by the inner fibration $q$; likewise for $i^*Y'$ and $Y'$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.2 opening base-replacement argument; inner-horn cell generation and quasicategory conventions

proof.text: Quasicategory of sections. Let $p:E\to S$ be any inner fibration of simplicial sets and $a:K\to S$ a small map, and put $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(K,E)_n=\{s:K\times\Delta^n\to E\mid ps=a\operatorname{pr}_K\}$. An inner horn $\Lambda^n_j\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(K,E)$ is a map $K\times\Lambda^n_j\to E$ over $a\operatorname{pr}_K$; the inclusion $K\times\Lambda^n_j\to K\times\Delta^n$ is the pushout-product of $\varnothing\to K$ with the inner anodyne $\Lambda^n_j\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, hence inner anodyne by the inner-anodyne pushout-product theorem, and $p$ supplies the filler over $a\operatorname{pr}_K$. Applied to $(q,\mathrm{id}_X)$, $(q',i)$ and $(q',\mathrm{id}_{X'})$ this shows that $\Gamma(q)$, $\Gamma(i^*q')=\operatorname{Fun}_{/X'}(X,Y')$ and $\Gamma(q')$ are quasicategories; no quasicategory hypothesis on $X$ or $Y$ is used. (For the last two, the relative functor-category statement gives the same conclusion.) Lifting for restriction. For a small parameter simplicial set $A$, a map $X'\times A\to Y'$ over $X'$ is a family of sections, and a map $X\times A\to i^*Y'$ over $X$ is the same as a map $X\times A\to Y'$ over $i\operatorname{pr}_X$. Given a square for a monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$, the two maps glue to the pushout $(X'\times A)\amalg_{X\times A}(X\times B)$. Its map to $X'\times B$ is the pushout-product of $i$ with $A\hookrightarrow B$, hence is inner anodyne by the inner-anodyne pushout-product theorem, and the inner fibration $q'$ supplies an extension over $\operatorname{pr}_{X'}$. Therefore $i^*:\Gamma(q')\to\Gamma(i^*q')$ has the right lifting property against every monomorphism, i.e. it is a trivial fibration of the Joyal model structure, hence a categorical equivalence between quasicategories. A categorical equivalence between quasicategories is a functor equivalence: test the defining equivalences $h\operatorname{Fun}(-,C)$ with $C=\Gamma(q')$ and $C=\Gamma(i^*q')$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.2 opening restriction argument, expanded by the internal-functor pushout-product calculation

proof.text: Choose the coherent inverse $v:i^*Y'\to Y$ over $X$ and the two coherent natural equivalences supplied in the hypothesis. Postcomposition gives $u_*:\Gamma(q)\to\Gamma(i^*q')$ and $v_*$ in the other direction; postcomposing the two displayed equivalences gives coherent natural equivalences $v_*u_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $u_*v_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Thus $u_*$ is a functor equivalence. The relative functor construction is the internal simplicial mapping construction, so these are equivalences on all higher simplices, not merely on vertices.

source.place: HTT 5.4.4.2, comparison map and coherent inverse

proof.text: For every vertex $x$ of $X$, restriction to the fiber gives $u_x:Y_x\to Y'_{i(x)}$. Restricting $u,v$ and their coherent inverse equations to the degree-zero fiber gives quasi-inverse functors and coherent natural equivalences, so $u_x$ is a fiber equivalence. The evaluation identities are strict identities of restrictions: $\operatorname{ev}_x(u_*s)=u_x(\operatorname{ev}_xs)$ and $\operatorname{ev}_x(i^*t)=\operatorname{ev}_{i(x)}t$. Hence the quasi-inverses produce the asserted coherent evaluation squares.

Fix an old edge $e:x\to z$ of $X$ and pull back along $e:\Delta^1\to X$: $Y_e=Y\times_X\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ and $Y'_e=Y'\times_{X'}\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ (via $i e$). These are inner fibrations over the quasicategory $\Delta^1$, so $Y_e,Y'_e$ are quasicategories, and an edge of $Y$ over $e$ that is $q$-cocartesian is cocartesian for the pullback, because a horn lifting problem over $\Delta^1$ composes to one over $X$ and the filler over $X$ together with the given map to $\Delta^n\to\Delta^1$ is a filler in the pullback; hence $Y_e\to\Delta^1$ and $Y'_e\to\Delta^1$ are cocartesian fibrations of quasicategories, with fibers $Y_x,Y_z$ and $Y'_{i(x)},Y'_{i(z)}$. The map $u$ restricts to $u_e:Y_e\to Y'_e$ over $\Delta^1$, preserving these cocartesian edges. Choose cocartesian transports $F_e:Y_x\to Y_z$ and $F'_e:Y'_{i(x)}\to Y'_{i(z)}$ with their coherent lifts $\lambda,\lambda'$ (pointwise cocartesian transport with $K=Y_x$, resp. $K=Y'_{i(x)}$). Then $u_e\lambda$ is a coherent transformation from $Y_x\to Y'_e$ (the composite $u_x$) to $u_zF_e$ with cocartesian components over $e$, and $\lambda'u_x$ is another such lift of the same transformation with target $F'_eu_x$. By the pointwise transport statement both are cocartesian edges of $\operatorname{Fun}(Y_x,Y'_e)$ over the same edge, so the universal comparison is an equivalence $F'_eu_x\simeq u_zF_e$ in the fiber $\operatorname{Fun}(Y_x,Y'_{i(z)})$, i.e. a coherent natural equivalence. On each morphism $g:y\to y'$ of $Y_x$, the cocartesian transport-square lemma applied in $Y'_e$ to $R=u_e\lambda_y$, $T=u_e\lambda_{y'}$, the morphism $u_x g$ and the image under $u_e$ of the naturality square of $\lambda$ at $g$ gives the compatibility $u_zF_e(g)\,c_R\simeq c_T\,F'_e(u_xg)$ of these comparisons, with all higher coherences retained. Thus the fiber equivalences intertwine transport on every old edge.

Inner horn inclusions $\Lambda^n_j\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ ($n\ge2$) are bijective on vertices, so pushouts of coproducts of them and countable composites add no vertices; as $i$ is a monomorphism, every vertex of $X'$ is $i(x)$ for a unique old vertex $x$, and the fiber of $q'$ over $i(x)$ equals $(i^*Y')_x$. Let $J\in\mathcal J$ and $D:J\to Y'_{i(x)}$, and let $v_x$ be the quasi-inverse of $u_x$ from Step 4. By hypothesis $v_xD$ has a colimiting cocone $\mu$ in $Y_x$. Since $u_x$ is an equivalence it induces equivalences of all mapping spaces, and of the coherent cocone spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,-)}(G,\Delta_Jc)$, so $u_x\mu$ is colimiting: the initial-object criterion of colimits in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] is invariant under such equivalences. The coherent equivalence $u_xv_xD\simeq D$ is an equivalence edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(J,Y'_{i(x)})$, and composing $u_x\mu$ with it gives a colimiting cocone on $D$ by the colimit-cocone transport lemma. Therefore every fiber of $q'$ admits every $J$-indexed colimit for $J\in\mathcal J$. The same two facts show that a functor coherently equivalent to a composite of colimit-preserving functors and equivalences preserves these colimits.

source.place: HTT 5.4.4.2 fiberwise transfer; coherent cocone criterion

proof.text: Write $X=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots$, $X'=\bigcup_mX_m$, each $X_{m+1}$ a pushout of a coproduct of inner horn inclusions along $X_m$. Inductive claim $P(m)$: for every edge $e$ of $X_m$, a (any) transport $F'_e$ of $q'$ along $e$ preserves the $J$-indexed colimits, $J\in\mathcal J$. Base $P(0)$: for an old edge, Step 5 gives $F'_e\simeq u_zF_ev_x$ with $F_e$ colimit preserving by hypothesis and $u_z,v_x$ equivalences, so $F'_e$ preserves them by Step 6. Inductive step: an edge of $X_{m+1}$ not in $X_m$ is the image of an edge of some attached $\Delta^n$ not in $\Lambda^n_j$. For $n\ge3$ every edge $\{a,b\}$ of $\Delta^n$ lies in a face $d_k$, $k\notin\{a,b\}$, $k\neq j$, hence in the horn, so only cells with $n=2$, $j=1$ add edges, and the new edge $w$ is the long edge of a $2$-simplex $\sigma$ of $X_{m+1}$ whose edges $e_1,e_2$ lie in $X_m$. For $y\in Y'$ over the source, take a cocartesian lift $\alpha$ of $e_1$ and a cocartesian lift $\beta$ of $e_2$ from its target, fill the inner horn $(\alpha,\beta)$ over $\sigma$ by the inner fibration $q'$ (with $X'$, $Y'$ quasicategories), and the long edge is cocartesian by the composition statement. By the coherent composition clause of pointwise transport, $F'_w\simeq F'_{e_2}F'_{e_1}$ coherently; both factors preserve the colimits by $P(m)$, so $F'_w$ does by Step 6. Every edge of $X'$ lies in some $X_m$, since the colimit is computed degreewise. Hence every edge transport of $q'$ preserves the transferred $J$-indexed colimits; degenerate edges have transports equivalent to the identity.

source.place: HTT Proposition 2.3.2.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.7, new-edge induction in the horn completion

proof.text: The preceding equivalences and transport comparisons prove all three asserted conclusions simultaneously: $\Gamma(q)$, $\Gamma(i^*q')$ and $\Gamma(q')$ are quasicategories; $u_*$ and $i^*$ are functor equivalences with the stated lifting property; evaluations and old-edge transports commute up to the displayed coherent equivalences; and the fiberwise colimit and transport hypotheses pass to $q'$. No filteredness condition has been introduced, so the final clause is exactly the stated scope.

proof_origin.place: Expanded proof of HTT Lemma 5.4.4.2 opening base-replacement argument, with HTT 2.3.2.4, 2.4.1.7 and 5.4.4.2; online source not archived in literature/.
